title: Etale near a closed subset gives an etale principal localization
statement: Let $A\to B$ be a homomorphism of commutative rings and $\mathfrak b\subseteq B$ an ideal. Assume that for every prime ideal $\mathfrak q\subset B$ with $\mathfrak b\subseteq\mathfrak q$ there is $h\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$ such that $\operatorname{Spec}B_h\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Then there is $g\in B$ whose image in $B/\mathfrak b$ is a unit such that $\operatorname{Spec}B_g\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07M0 (lemma-localize-upstairs, line 1821) and its proof (the non-etale locus is closed, V(J') with V(J') ∩ V(J) empty, Algebra Lemma 00E0 lemma-Zariski-topology, 1 = f + g with f in J, g in J')

proof.text: Let $G=\{h\in B:\operatorname{Spec}B_h\to\operatorname{Spec}A\text{ is etale}\}$ and let $J'\subseteq B$ be the ideal generated by $G$. Then $V(J')=\{\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}B: G\subseteq\mathfrak q\}$ is the closed set of primes $\mathfrak q$ admitting no $h\in B\setminus\mathfrak q$ with $\operatorname{Spec}B_h\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ etale (the non-etale locus; its complement $\bigcup_{h\in G}D(h)$ is open, as for the smooth locus in [def-weil-pbc-singular-ideal]). By hypothesis every prime $\mathfrak q\supseteq\mathfrak b$ has some $h\in G$ with $h\notin\mathfrak q$, so $\mathfrak q\notin V(J')$. Hence $V(J')\cap V(\mathfrak b)=\emptyset$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M0 (lemma-localize-upstairs, line 1821), sentences 1-3 ('The set of points ... is a closed subset', 'Write this as V(J')', 'V(J') ∩ V(J) = ∅'); Stacks takes for the closedness Algebra, Definition 00U1 (definition-etale), whose 'etale at q' is exactly the hypothesis here

proof.text: By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-zero-loci-disjoint-unit-ideal] applied to $\mathfrak b$ and $J'$, $\mathfrak b+J'=B$: write $1=f+g$ with $f\in\mathfrak b$ and $g\in J'$. Then $g\equiv1\pmod{\mathfrak b}$, so the image of $g$ in $B/\mathfrak b$ is the unit $1$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M0 (lemma-localize-upstairs, line 1821), 'hence J + J' = B by Algebra, Lemma 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology). Write 1 = f + g with f in J and g in J''

proof.text: It remains to see that $\operatorname{Spec}B_g\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale (Stacks: 'Then $g$ works'). Since $g\in J'$, $g=\sum_{i=1}^n c_ih_i$ with $n\ge0$, $c_i\in B$, $h_i\in G$. In $B_g$ the element $g/1$ is a unit, so $\sum_i (c_i/g)(h_i/1)=1$: the elements $h_1/1,\dots,h_n/1$ generate the unit ideal of $B_g$, and by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] (i) the principal opens $U_i=D(h_i/1)$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}B_g$. (If $n=0$ then $g=0$, $B_g=0$ and $\operatorname{Spec}B_g$ is empty, covered by the empty family.)

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07M0 (lemma-localize-upstairs, line 1821), last sentence 'Then g works', written out: g lies in the ideal generated by the h with B_h etale, so D(g) is covered by the D(g h_i)

proof.text: Fix $i$ and let $C_i=(B_g)_{h_i/1}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] the morphism $\psi_i:\operatorname{Spec}C_i\to\operatorname{Spec}B_g$ induced by the localization map is an open immersion with image $U_i$, so by [def-weil-open-immersion] $\psi_i=j_i\circ\varphi_i$ with $\varphi_i:\operatorname{Spec}C_i\to U_i$ an isomorphism onto the open subscheme $U_i$ and $j_i:U_i\to\operatorname{Spec}B_g$ the inclusion. The ring $C_i$, with $B\to B_g\to C_i$, is a localization of $B$ at the multiplicative set $\{g^ah_i^b\}$, and so is $(B_{h_i})_{g/1}$ with $B\to B_{h_i}\to(B_{h_i})_{g/1}$; by the universal property of localization the $B$-algebra map $B_{h_i}\to C_i$, $x/h_i^b\mapsto x/(g^0h_i^b)$, identifies $C_i$ with $(B_{h_i})_{g/1}$, and the two composites $A\to B\to B_g\to C_i$ and $A\to B\to B_{h_i}\to C_i$ agree. Hence $\pi\circ\psi_i$, with $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}B_g\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ the structure morphism, equals the composite $\operatorname{Spec}C_i\to\operatorname{Spec}B_{h_i}\to\operatorname{Spec}A$. The first map is induced by a principal localization of $B_{h_i}$, so it is an open immersion [lem-weil-pbc-principal-localization-open-immersion] and hence etale ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1)); the second is etale since $h_i\in G$. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2), $\pi\circ\psi_i$ is etale.

proof.text: For each $i$, $\pi\circ j_i=(\pi\circ\psi_i)\circ\varphi_i^{-1}$, and $\varphi_i^{-1}:U_i\to\operatorname{Spec}C_i$ is an isomorphism, hence an open immersion [def-weil-open-immersion], hence etale ([lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (1)); so $\pi\circ j_i$ is etale by step 4 and [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation] (2). Since the $U_i$ cover $\operatorname{Spec}B_g$ (step 3), [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source] shows that $\pi:\operatorname{Spec}B_g\to\operatorname{Spec}A$ is etale. Together with step 2, $g$ is as required.
